description.narrative: This investment consolidated several activities focused on supporting the COVID-19 pandemic response in PNG. It included support to (1) NGO’s to rapidly scale up existing programming to reduce the risk of COVID-19 community transmission and assist in the rollout of vaccines (Australian Humanitarian Partnership); (2) Laboratory Strengthening and procurement and distribution of GeneXpert and rapid antigen testing; (3) AUSMAT Team deployments to PNG to support its response to COVID-19 Delta Variant Surge Outbreak; (4) Provision of medical supplies, transport/storage, supply and provision of PPE, and additional AUSMAT-specific supplies; logistics support for Critical Response Teams, AUSMAT and NZMAT team members (5) PNG COVID-19 vaccines roll out through ISOS; (6) Deployment of Australian clinicians into the PNG hospital system; and (7) COVID-19 communications research.

description.narrative: In 2022-23, the COVID Clinical Support Project deployed 26 Australian and New Zealand clinicians to PNG, from the emergency medicine, intensive care and midwifery disciplines. In partnership with Australian medical colleges and other specialist societies, these clinicians were deployed to both Port Moresby General Hospital and ANGAU Memorial Provincial Hospital, supporting their Papua New Guinean peers to strengthen their response to COVID-19, and prepare for future potential outbreaks of infectious diseases.

The COVID-19 Clinical Support Project from February 2022 to December 2023 rapidly deployed Australian technical experts across PNG to support the COVID-19 clinical response. In this reporting period, 188 PNG clinicians benefited from training on critical care skills, leadership, triage, and respectful maternity care - with a cross-cutting focus on infection prevention and control. The project contributed to improved clinical capacity across the PNG health system and bolstered preparedness for future infectious disease outbreaks. A train the trainer methodology was used to enhance sustainability and ownership of skills and knowledge. The project demonstrated the value of a peer-to-peer model of clinical support and knowledge exchange.
